analysis.title: [GSX] Global Reflections
key_insights: Post-midterm relief reversed on 11/5 and the market went back into AI panic mode. Frequent swings between AI and non-AI trades have cut conviction, and prime data shows de-grossing in eight of the last nine sessions.
GS recommends shorting US Staples (GSXUSTAP). The defensive rotation made sense in October but now looks stretched relative to fundamentals.
The vol panic index hit 9.57 out of 10 on 11/5, the biggest 2-day round trip on record. Cboe posted its largest put volume day on record.
The US broad AI basket (GSTMTAIP) had its worst day since March 2020. The unconstrained TMT momentum pair (GSTMTMOM) posted its tenth -10pp day this year.
Global equities have seen de-grossing for four straight sessions. Net selling was the largest in two weeks (-1.6 SDs over 1 year), with long sales 2.2x short sales.

Fundamental L/S net leverage (beta-adjusted) fell 7.6pts w/w to 57.2%, down 14.1pts YTD and the lowest since May 2025 (4th percentile 3Y, 19th percentile 5Y). Overall Prime book net leverage is at the 4th percentile on a 1Y view and the 37th percentile on a 5Y view.
As positioning nears washout levels, GS likes owning the rebound in Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR), where it sees the largest long-term AI monetization potential.

Asia AI followed the US lower. Clients added downside protection via Taiwan Tech hedges and sold short in Korea and Japan. China Domestic AI held up better, helped by policy support and national-team buying.
GS favors re-engaging via GS China Domestic AI (GSXACADO) after the correction, citing compressed valuations and continued momentum behind domestic substitution.
Defensives in the US and Europe just had their best monthly performance spread versus the market on record. GS says fundamentals do not justify the valuation re-rate.
US Staples trade at their highest valuation premium to SPX in 10+ years. The dividend yield is 200bps below the US 10Y and earnings growth does not justify the valuation.
European Staples (GSXESTAP) dividend yield is 100bp above US peers, but the group has also re-rated beyond earnings (16x PE, 90th percentile over 1 year).
Energy prices reflect higher odds of a US-Iran peace deal. Brent is below $100/bbl and European gas (TTF) fell 17% on the week to about EUR86/MWh.

The European Hormuz Bottleneck basket (GSXEHRMZ) is up 30% since end February and trades 25% above its 5y multiple (10x PE). Consensus expects 75% of the basket to post declining EPS over the next 2 years, and GS says the earnings gains came from temporary factors that should reverse in a peace outcome.
GS recommends limited-loss implementations for an Iran resolution because of the tail risk to the trade.
Equities had their worst 1-day performance since Liberation Day, but credit spreads stayed resilient. The generic 30y spread widened 2.2bps against the 8bp implied by the 4.4% SPX drop.

GS credit structuring argues credit downside convexity has not kicked in yet and that credit would underperform equity in a systematic risk-off. It recommends shorting the generic IG 30Y basket against a beta-weighted long S&P future.
